title: Candidate continuity checklist and remote handoff protocol
body:
Purpose:
Provide a compact, practical checklist that ensures candidate context, interview evidence, and operational tasks are transferred reliably from recruiting → hiring manager → people ops → mentor for remote hires. This doc is intended to reduce first-week noise, preserve interview signals for calibration, and create an explicit 7-day mentor sprint for ramping remote hires quickly.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Capture interview evidence at offer time (not later).
- Use single canonical handoff card (HR ticket) with required fields below.
- Ship equipment and enable critical access before Day 1 (VPN, email, first-repo).
- Pair the new hire with a 7-day mentor sprint with daily micro-goals and async check-ins.

Owner / point people:
- Document owner: Sofia Ramirez (people-ops)
- Recruiting owner (pre-offer): Ava Patel
- Hiring manager: Michael Chen
- Mentor lead: Priya Desai

Triggers (status changes that invoke this checklist):
- Offer extended (recruiting -> create handoff card)
- Offer accepted (start procurement + access tasks)
- Day -5 (confirm shipping/tracking + calendar invites)
- Day 0 (welcome + legal/compliance)

Handoff card required fields (create in HR ticketing system):
- Candidate name, role, level, start date, timezone
- Hiring manager + mentor names + emails
- Interview summary (3 bullet signals + strongest risk) — mandatory
- Code exercise artifacts (link) or take-home notes (if any)
body_2:
- Tech stack access required (repo list, infra, cloud projects)
- Security clearance / NDA status
- Equipment list + shipping address + tracking number
- Payroll details entered (local forms)

Interview evidence capture (at offer time):
- 3x sentence summary: What stood out / what to watch for.
- Skill rubric mapping (quick table): Skill | Signal examples | Evidence link | Risk flag (Y/N)
- Example entries (copy into handoff card):
  * System design: clear trade-offs on caching vs consistency; gave latency estimation with back-of-envelope. Evidence: confluence/design-238. Risk: None.
  * Python/infra: wrote clean testable snippet; used async primitives correctly. Evidence: candidate-repo/commit. Risk: Might need pairing on our infra libs.
- Decision rationale: include hiring manager "why hire" 1–2 sentences (this is a compliance artifact for later calibration).

Operational checklist (Offer accepted → Day -5):
- Recruiting: mark offer accepted in ATS; create HR handoff card with all required fields.
- People Ops: open procurement ticket for equipment (laptop + peripherals) and add expedited shipping if start < 7 days.
- IT: create mail alias, Slack account, core SSO SAML entry (provision disabled until Day 0)
- Security: generate temporary VPN/Okta invite and include onboarding MFA steps
- Manager: add new hire to team calendar, create Day 1 orientation invite (45m) and 1:1 repeating for 30/60/90
- Mentor: accept pairing; block 30–60m for Day 1 pairing + daily async check-ins for week 1
- Documentation: paste interview evidence summary into the handoff card (exact copy), link to code samples

Day -2 → Day 0 (final checks):
- Confirm equipment tracking + confirm battery + power adapter present.
- Confirm onboarding docs link and first-week reading list have been emailed.
- Manager ensures first PR/first small task is ready to be assigned Day 2.
- Mentor schedules Day 1 1:1 and 30m pairing session Day 2.

7-day Mentor Sprint (remote-focused):
Goal: first sprint reduces ambiguity, guarantees first small wins, and surfaces blockers early. Mentor does less heavy-tasking, more scaffolding.
- Day 0 (welcome): 45m intro (team norms, communication channels, high-level product), quick tour of repos, safety (who to ping when things break).
- Day 1: environment + local build + run sample app (mentor watches or pairs). Aim: produce a local run success message.
- Day 2: small bug or docs change PR assigned; mentor reviews PR same day.
- Day 3: integrate with simple infra flow (e.g., run a test pipeline or deploy to sandbox) — mentor provides checklist.
- Day 4: onboarding retro (30m) — what was confusing, what changes to docs; update onboarding docs immediately.
- Day 5: cross-team intro + small demo of what was learned; manager reviews progress and adjusts next steps.
- Day 6: ramp plan handoff — new hire proposes next 30 days goals with mentor feedback.

Remote-specific handoff details (logistics + soft signals):
- Timezone confirmation: explicitly state core overlap hours (at least 3 hours) and preferred async windows.
- Home office checklist sent with equipment: do you need monitor stand, international power adapter? (flag in handoff card)
- Video-first onboarding: ensure camera + background check; encourage test call on Day -1 to avoid Day 1 delays.
- Social onboarding: allocate 15m intro with one cross-functional partner Day 3 to create lateral context.

Interview rubric addendum (compact, to be pasted into ATS/handoff):
- Scores: 1 (no evidence), 2 (partial), 3 (meets expectations), 4 (above), 5 (exceptional).
- Core dimensions: Problem solving, System design, Code quality, Communication, Team fit, Learning velocity.
- Required artifact links: code samples / design doc / take-home repo (must be linked in handoff card).
- Manager note: include explicit coaching areas (1–2 bullets) to prioritize first 30 days.

Common failure modes (notes-to-self):
- Recruiting forgets to paste interview evidence (most frequent) — mitigate with template copy/paste field mandatory.
- Hardware shipped but wrong adapter/regulatory form missing; escalate procurement to expedited vendor.
- Mentor overloaded: assign fallback mentor and state expected weekly time commitment (3–4 hours first week).

Risks and open questions (for review):
- How to handle international tax forms faster than standard 2-week timeline? (Action: finance to propose fast-path)
- Do managers consistently use the rubric? We need a monthly calibration runway.

Templates / quick copy snippets (paste into handoff card):
- 3-line interview summary (required): Example: Strong backend engineer; clear ownership & pragmatic trade-offs; risk: unfamiliar with our infra libs — pair for first two weeks.
- Mandatory fields checklist (checkbox to paste): Interview summary, Artifacts links, Manager rationale, Mentor assigned, Equipment address, Payroll details.

Links / references: (patch these into the handoff ticket)
- Onboarding reading list: confluence:ONBOARD-READLIST-2025
- Interview rubric master: confluence:HIRING-RUBRIC-CORE
- ATS handoff template: github:repo/onboarding-templates/blob/main/handoff-template.md

Next steps / action items (short):
- People Ops: make handoff card template mandatory in ATS (owner: Sofia) — due: 2025-10-09
- Recruiting: start copying interview evidence at offer time (owner: Ava) — immediate
- Managers: accept mentor pairing within 48 hours of offer acceptance (owner: Michael) — immediate

Appendix: quick checklist for managers to paste into calendar invite body:
- Welcome note + team norms link
- First small task (link) + expected outcome by Day 5
- Mentor contact + 1:1 cadence + core overlap hours

(End)

Notes: this is intentionally compact to fit into a single HR ticket body. Keep language actionable; avoid long narrative. Will iterate after two hires run through this flow and we gather feedback.

Unresolved: need to instrument a tiny NPS / 1–3 quick questions to send after Day 7 and Day 30 — suggestions welcome.
footnote: workspace: Google Drive — working doc (mix of checklist + copy snippets). This is a people-ops working draft — not final policy.
